compiled_state.title: [ticket-cli]: ticket show/transition/comment with Jira-style ID -> 'ticket not found' error
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
### 1. Technical Environment

* **code_version:** e68f7ce4fbb33675dc778dd15cff4c2bc5d81911

### 2. Incident Overview

* **Scenario Type:** User-Flagged Behavior

#### Expected Behavior

`ticket show <id>`, `ticket transition <id> ...`, and other ticket CLI commands should work with Jira-style ticket IDs (e.g. `jira-dig-2529`) the same as UUID-style IDs (e.g. `1d42-ffcb-e5a6-4594`). Tickets with Jira-style IDs live in the local ticket system and can be operated on normally.

#### Actual Behavior

`.claude/scripts/dso ticket show jira-dig-2529` returns exit code 1 with `Error: ticket 'jira-dig-2529' not found`, even though the ticket exists on the tickets orphan branch (confirmed via git log showing COMPACT, STATUS, and COMMENT events for jira-dig-2529). The agent also incorrectly concluded that Jira-style IDs are purely Jira-side references with no local presence.

### 3. Action History

1. Agent ran `ticket show jira-dig-2529` — exit 1, ticket not found
2. Agent ran `ticket list --format=llm` and searched for jira/dig patterns — returned empty
3. `git log --all --oneline | grep jira-dig-2529` confirmed events exist on the tickets branch
4. User confirmed the ticket lives locally and the CLI should be able to find it

### 6. Logs

```
$ .claude/scripts/dso ticket show jira-dig-2529
Error: ticket 'jira-dig-2529' not found
Exit code: 1

$ git log --all --oneline | grep jira-dig-2529
2af672f135 ticket: COMPACT jira-dig-2529
e36ab81f60 ticket: STATUS jira-dig-2529
6228bcd395 ticket: COMMENT jira-dig-2529
45537f5ce4 fix(jira-dig-2529): detect BEHIND mergeStateStatus in _phase_poll
a97203c420 ticket: COMMENT jira-dig-2529
```

comments.body: Additional diagnostic: ticket transition DOES recognize the Jira-style ID — it correctly reports the current status. Only ticket show (and likely ticket list/exists) fail to recognize it. Run: '.claude/scripts/dso ticket transition jira-dig-2529 in_progress closed' returns 'Error: current status is "closed", not "in_progress"' — proving (a) the ticket exists locally, (b) it's already closed, (c) transition can find it. The bug is scoped to the show/list lookup path, not the transition or update path.
comments.author: Test

comments.body: CLUSTER: same root cause as 2eea-e443-270c-4e92 — ticket CLI lookup path is fragmented across commands (transition uses one resolver, show/comment use another, list normalization differs). Fix should centralize ID resolution into a single helper that accepts: (a) UUID short-form like 1d42-ffcb, (b) UUID full-form like 1d42-ffcb-e5a6-4594, (c) Jira-style like jira-dig-2529, (d) user-friendly alias like slid-opera-cabin. Every ticket command should call the central resolver and inherit consistent error contracts (including JSON-on-error so orchestrator parsing does not break).
comments.author: Test

comments.body: Classification: behavioral, cluster scored BASIC (max-of-tier=2). Cluster members: 023d-2d40-e099-4b97 (P2, CLI lookup-path inconsistency on jira-style IDs) + 2eea-e443-270c-4e92 (P3, non-JSON error contract on ticket show miss). Intent Gate: skipped — CLI_user tag present on both.
comments.author: Test

comments.body:
AUDIT (broader hardening sweep — beyond initial cluster scope):

ID-resolution bypass surface in production code:

(1) ticket-lib-api.sh — _ticketlib_resolve_short_id only handles 8-hex; silently passes through jira-style/alias inputs unchanged. Used by EIGHT API functions (sub-agent identified four; audit found four more):
  - ticket_comment ✗
  - ticket_tag ✗
  - ticket_untag ✗
  - ticket_edit ✗
  - ticket_set_file_impact ✗ (NEW)
  - ticket_get_file_impact ✗ (NEW)
  - ticket_archive ✗ (NEW)
  - ticket_delete ✗ (NEW)

(2) ticket-lib.sh — ticket_read_status does raw dir check, no resolution. Called by ticket-transition.sh, ticket-create.sh, ticket-link.sh, ticket-lib-api.sh:ticket_create. ticket_transition appearing to 'work' for jira-style IDs is COINCIDENCE — the literal directory .tickets-tracker/jira-dig-2529/ happens to exist; it would fail for an alias or a jira_key whose canonical dir is the UUID form.

(3) Standalone scripts (ticket-show.sh, ticket-comment.sh, ticket-edit.sh, ticket-link.sh, ticket-transition.sh, ticket-create.sh) — all do raw dir checks. Direct callers are only TESTS; production goes through ticket-lib-api.sh. Defensive resolve_ticket_id call is desirable for hardening but lower priority.

Other shared-helper bypasses audited — NONE FOUND:
  - write_commit_event: consistently used by ticket-comment/create/edit. ticket-compact inlines git ops with documented rationale (flock nesting).
  - _tag_add / _tag_remove: correctly invoked.
  - Event-file writes: routed through write_commit_event.

Expanded fix plan:
  Phase A. Add _ticketlib_resolve_id in ticket-lib-api.sh — single helper handling 8-hex, 16-hex, jira_key, alias, prefix. Source of truth lives in ticket-lib.sh::resolve_ticket_id; the API-layer helper is a thin wrapper that picks the fast hex path first.
  Phase B. Replace _ticketlib_resolve_short_id calls in all 8 API functions with _ticketlib_resolve_id.
  Phase C. Replace raw dir checks in remaining API functions (ticket_create, etc.) with _ticketlib_resolve_id calls where the input is a user-provided ID (NOT for self-create where the canonical ID was just generated).
  Phase D. Update ticket_read_status in ticket-lib.sh to call resolve_ticket_id internally so ticket_transition becomes correct by design rather than coincidence.
  Phase E. Update ticket_show error contract — emit JSON on stdout with {error,input,message} on lookup miss + non-zero exit; preserve human stderr message (bug 2eea fix).
  Phase F. RED tests covering: jira-style ID for each of the 8 API functions + JSON error contract on miss + ticket_read_status resolution.
